correctness.rationale: The hypotheses are exactly full stars and triangles. The all-positive trace excludes disjoint pairs; for four edges at a common center, marking three positive forces the full star and cannot exclude the fourth. For either type of triple the proof has all eight witnesses, including the triangle of the leaves for the zero trace on a star and an outside star for the zero trace on a triangle; both work at n=4. Counting gives the stated f-polynomial and purity. Following any first positive answer, the next positive branch of any nonconstant query has at most two concepts, insufficient for a remaining depth of two in a putative depth-four tree. The star two-skeleta are simply connected; their singleton overlaps underlie K_n. Each added triangle kills the corresponding triangular loop, and those based at a fixed vertex normally generate the graph's fundamental group. Thus the two-dimensional complex is simply connected; Euler characteristic gives B_n, and Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the wedge of spheres. Inclusion in the full complex kills the extra n binom(n−2,3) classes: each full star simplex fills its own two-skeleton cycles, which have rank binom(n−2,3), with disjoint triangle supports across distinct stars. At n=4 there are no extra cycles of this kind.
residual_risks: The independent computation is finite and does not certify integral homotopy. The integral claim and uniformity in n follow from the proof, not the frozen mod-two ranks.

evidence: Frankl–Kupavskii bound numbers of maximal intersecting families. Goyal–Shukla–Singh §3 treat full clique complexes of line graphs and obtain a wedge result for connected chordal host graphs.
Their full line-graph complex relates to the two-skeleton of the host graph's own clique complex, not the two-skeleton of the line-graph clique complex.

value.rationale: The claim identifies all membership supports in a canonical unbounded family and gives a uniform adaptive limit despite the growing number of concepts. The truncation changes the second Betti rank from order n³ to order n⁴ while preserving purity and simple connectivity. This quantifies the difference between structural feasibility of positive edges and full realizability of patterns, an invariant useful for comparison with other maximal-clique models.
residual_risks: Restricted to pair membership on maximal intersecting 2-sets; no higher uniformity or general host-graph theorem follows.
